dplyr: filter()

filter() keeps only the rows that meet a condition. Choose a cut and a minimum carat and see which rows survive.

viewof site = Inputs.select(site_options, {label: "Site"})
viewof min_date = Inputs.select(date_options, {label: "Earliest date"})
rows = transpose(choices)
match = rows.find(d => d.site === site && d.min_date === min_date)

The code:

{
const pre = document.createElement("pre");
pre.className = "plot-code";
const code = document.createElement("code");
code.textContent = match.code;
pre.appendChild(code);
return pre;
}

The result:

{
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.className = "side-by-side";
  wrap.innerHTML =
    "<div><p><b>Before</b> (green = kept, struck-through = dropped)</p>" + match.before + "</div>" +
    "<div><p><b>After</b></p>" + match.after + "</div>";
  return wrap;
}
